title: Why unlabeled graph matching misidentified alanine
description: Early molfind assigned this fragment to alanine after matching its formula and unlabeled graph shape. (A) Element colors reveal different chemical connectivity. (B) Hiding element identity illustrates the false positive. The correction required categorical atom-element and bonded-element-pair matching. GPU pipelines can screen candidates with counts or fingerprints, but named identities require element-aware connectivity verification.
note: Both panels show the fragment incorrectly matched as alanine. Dissertation §5.1.2 / Fig. 5-2 (pp. 103–104) and Appendix D (p. 129) document the early NetworkX error and its correction. Unlabeled isomorphism checks graph shape, not just atom/bond totals. The exact matcher ran on CPU in the GPU-accelerated workflow; hardware did not cause the failure. Edge labels were element pairs, not recovered bond orders/charge/stereochemistry. Original panel images remain available below; no source deletion or molecular redraw.
